open_points.subject: M26 EffectAttempt vs K-08 approval policy
open_points.text: K-08: "At run time each `state-transition`, `external-effect` and `destructive` node stops for the owner's approval..." and M26: "...except a resend after `not_applied`, which, whatever its class, records the fresh approval it needed;"
open_points.question: If a `draft-write` attempt is resolved `not_applied`, must the resend now require an explicit owner approval (creating `owner_approval` waiting), or does `draft-write` remain approval-free even on resend?
options: Resend of `draft-write` after `not_applied` requires fresh owner approval.
`draft-write` never requires per-attempt approval; "fresh approval" applies only to classes that already stop for approval.
open_points.default_guess: Require fresh owner approval for any class on resend after `not_applied`, because M26 states "whatever its class".

open_points.subject: M10 ManifestOperation instance facts when no instance is selected
open_points.text: M10 defines `base_url` as "the manifest's base URL of the one instance the installation selects for the service"; it explicitly says `required_headers` and `instance_class` are absent when no instance is selected, but does not say whether `base_url` is absent too.
open_points.question: When `service_instances` has no selected instance for a service, what is the `ManifestOperation` fact set for `base_url`?
options: No `ManifestOperation` is read at all for that service/operation.
`base_url` is still populated from some default/source even without a selected instance.
open_points.default_guess: Treat `base_url` as absent when no instance is selected.

open_points.subject: M08 AdmissionVerdict creation/uniqueness across repeated submissions
open_points.text: M08 says "a verdict for the same implementation and corpus is the same verdict" and also says admission runs "every active case ... again ... at admission time" with fields including `trial_executions` and `decided_at`.
open_points.question: If the same implementation is submitted again with unchanged corpus, does the kernel create a new AdmissionVerdict (and new TrialExecutions), or reuse the existing verdict record?
options: Reuse one stored verdict per (`implementation_id`,`corpus_digest`); no new admission record.
Re-run admission and create a new verdict record each submission, even for same pair.
open_points.default_guess: Reuse one verdict per implementation+corpus pair.

open_points.subject: State 0 fixed action surface vs M22 file-byte read
open_points.text: K-11 fixes operations to "inspect, author, try, run, resume, read traces, and the owner's approve, accept, activate, grant, revoke, resolve and cancel"; M22 says spooled files are read by "the State 5 operation `read_spooled_file`".
open_points.question: Is reading spooled file bytes a separate product action (thus part of the fixed surface), or must it be served through existing inspect/read-trace actions, or not exposed at all?
options: Add explicit `read_spooled_file` action to the fixed MCP surface (owner-only).
Return file bytes via existing inspect/read-trace actions.
Do not expose spool-byte reading as a product action.
